candidates.summary: Indonesia's senior legal affairs minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra said Monday that the government was taking steps to prevent misuse of state surveillance equipment and would consider sweeping the presidential palace for bugging devices. His remarks followed the arrest last week of four senior police officers accused of unauthorized monitoring, including of President Prabowo Subianto. An investigation remained underway, with no formal charges announced.
candidates.title: Indonesia reviews surveillance controls after alleged wiretapping

candidates.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce announced Monday that the suspension of expanded export controls covering rare earths and other items would be extended for two months until January 10, 2027. The announcement preserves the pause in those measures rather than removing all Chinese rare-earth export controls.
candidates.title: China announces two-month extension of export-control suspension

candidates.summary: A World Meteorological Organization report released Monday said the January–September global average temperature was 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average. The report said ocean temperatures continued rising from 2025 record highs and global mean sea levels had reached a record this year. It assessed 2026 as on track to rank among the four hottest years recorded; that is a provisional assessment, not a completed annual result.
candidates.title: WMO releases provisional global climate assessment for 2026

candidates.summary: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met employers' organizations and private-sector unions Monday morning to discuss purchasing power and wages amid continuing cost-of-living protests. Unions sought increases in the minimum wage. At the time of the report, government measures remained to be announced; no new wage increase had been confirmed.
candidates.title: French prime minister holds cost-of-living talks with unions and employers

candidates.summary: Greece's coast guard said Monday that it recovered 13 bodies and 18 survivors from a boat spotted by a container ship off Crete early that morning. One of four survivors taken to hospital subsequently died, according to the coast guard. The cause of the deaths aboard the boat was not immediately clear; authorities said it may have been at sea for days in strong winds.
candidates.title: Greek coast guard recovers migrant boat off Crete; 14 reported dead

candidates.summary: Following Monday's talks with unions and employers, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced a planned 1.6% minimum-wage increase from December 1, bringing monthly net pay to approximately €1,502, about €24 more. A decree remained to be published; the increase was not yet in force. Lecornu also announced work on reforming employer social-security contribution reductions and proposed tax measures intended to support purchasing power.
candidates.title: French prime minister announces planned December minimum-wage increase

candidates.summary: The World Meteorological Organization released its provisional 2026 climate assessment Monday. January–September global average surface temperature was about 1.47°C above the pre-industrial average. The agency reported record sea levels and said 2026 was on track for a tenth successive year of record ocean warmth and to rank among the four warmest years recorded. These annual assessments remained provisional rather than completed full-year results.
candidates.title: WMO releases provisional global climate assessment for 2026

candidates.summary: The UN's COP31 climate conference opened Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, after a delayed opening ceremony. Negotiators had been discussing developing countries' demands to put climate-finance issues on the agenda. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for faster emissions cuts, a transition away from fossil fuels and financial support for vulnerable countries. The opening did not establish a negotiated agreement on those issues.
candidates.title: COP31 climate talks open in Antalya amid finance-agenda dispute

candidates.summary: Representative Thomas Massie introduced an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor Monday. The resolution alleges unlawful conduct involving military operations in Iran, Yemen and Venezuela. Hegseth rejected the effort as politically motivated. Introduction of the resolution did not constitute impeachment or removal; no House vote was reported.
candidates.title: Massie introduces resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth

candidates.summary: The Supreme Court granted a stay Monday of a lower-court injunction blocking border construction and associated legal waivers in Texas's Big Bend Sector. The Court said the government was highly likely to establish that the district court lacked jurisdiction over the challengers' statutory-authority claim. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson would have denied the application. The stay permits construction to proceed while further Supreme Court review is pursued; it is not a final merits judgment.
candidates.title: Supreme Court stays injunction blocking Big Bend border construction

sources.name: Supreme Court of the United States

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump told reporters Monday, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, that he believed the Iran war was militarily effectively over and described positive momentum toward ending it. He also said U.S. forces remained ready to act and that a long-term solution concerning Iran's nuclear program was still needed. The remarks did not announce a peace agreement or establish that hostilities had ended.
candidates.title: Trump signals reduced need for military action after meeting Qatari prime minister

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks closed sharply higher Monday: the S&P 500 rose 2.3% to 7,549.94, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 2.2% to 52,389.75, and the Nasdaq Composite increased 2.7% to 25,253.14. Brent crude fell 5.8% to $92.57 a barrel. Nvidia shares declined 4.3% despite the broader rally.
candidates.title: U.S. stock indexes rally as Brent crude falls

candidates.summary: Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman agreed Monday to open two additional crossings, coordinate emergency responses and share archival materials after meeting UN envoy Maria Angela Holguin in Nicosia. The UN described the meeting as positive and said further talks with Secretary-General António Guterres were planned. The agreement was a confidence-building development, not a settlement of the island's division.
candidates.title: Cyprus leaders agree on additional crossings and cooperation measures

candidates.summary: Representative Thomas Massie renewed his effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, reading an eight-article resolution on the House floor and invoking a procedure intended to force consideration. The resolution alleges unlawful conduct involving Iran and other military operations, civilian protections and retaliation against Senator Mark Kelly. It substantially repeats Massie's September resolution, whose consideration was interrupted by the congressional recess. Hegseth rejected the effort as politically motivated. No House vote on impeachment had occurred.
candidates.title: Massie renews Hegseth impeachment effort using privileged-resolution procedure

candidates.summary: The Senate voted 73–25 Monday to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the legislative vehicle for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act permitting package. The vote limited debate on whether to take up the vehicle; it did not pass the permitting legislation or put its provisions into effect.
candidates.title: Senate clears procedural hurdle for permitting legislation

candidates.summary: French officials on Monday attributed last month's cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems to an Iranian Revolutionary Guard-affiliated group. Paris prosecutors opened a formal judicial investigation, and Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador was being summoned and European sanctions would be sought. Authorities said the attack affected about 700 supermarkets. The attribution and investigation were Monday's developments; the refrigeration attack occurred in October. The announced sanctions were not yet enacted.
candidates.title: France attributes supermarket refrigeration cyberattack to Iranian group

candidates.summary: Novaya Gazeta closed its Moscow newsroom Monday after announcing on October 30 that pressure from Russian authorities and security services had forced it to cease operations. Journalists removed portraits of murdered colleagues during the office's final day. Authorities had blocked its online platforms, revoked its media registration and disrupted reader donations, according to AP. Novaya Gazeta Europe, established abroad by former staff, is a separate outlet.
candidates.title: Novaya Gazeta closes Moscow newsroom following government pressure

sources.name: Associated Press via The Times of Israel

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI was investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent. China denied the espionage allegation, calling it unsubstantiated. Democratic congressional leaders also sought further briefings. Nvidia had announced its independent investigation on Sunday, not Monday. Trump's remarks did not establish that espionage occurred or that Huang knowingly participated in it.
candidates.title: Trump says FBI is examining Huang affair; China denies espionage allegation
